# Intent

Make the existing OW47 two-stage corpus graph runnable through a source-pinned
BLUT standard cookbook, and integrate its truthful runtime evidence. The observed
provider failed to package a locator-only dataset; the repair retains owned bytes.
This is shared integration work, not a rewrite or resolution of signed OW47.

Out of scope: new graph semantics, relaxed artifact checks, copied lineage,
training/model calls, provider publication, SAS acceptance and assurance awards.

# Basis

The unchanged signed OW-WAR-0047 graph and obligations define the historical
runtime target. Its implementation/shared-materialization-contract.md is the one
shared adapter contract. Provider patch: Quitetall/blut-cookbooks PR #1, b10f46b;
provider source base 12d09c5d2f00ecf52394c11657c50b14bc04bb7c. Both original and
source-pinned failures remain under OW47 implementation/. Repaired runtime uses
locked BLUT engine ffecee56abc87175a55dedc9f92d3537fa5a4227.

Preparation, local tests and retained observations can proceed independently.
Integration needs provider checks and exact source identities; GitHub currently
refuses to start provider CI because of account billing/spending limits. That is
unavailable observation, not code failure. Account owner controls remediation.
OpenWarrant PR #118 is the parent integration branch, not an assurance prerequisite.

No authorization, judgment, disposition or signed OW47 source is replaced.

# Work Order

1. Retain original and source-pinned failure reproductions, exact inputs,
   dependency/binary identities and actual failed job status.
2. Integrate provider-owned materialization repair through its shared contract:
   owned copy, hash/count of copied bytes, atomic publication, source preservation,
   prior-output preservation on failure and changed cache behavior version.
3. Validate unchanged OW47 PlanSpec with actual two-stage execution, zero cache
   hits, output-byte comparison, status/artifact receipts and external lineage
   references. Exercise positive and incompatible-port controls through war CLI.
4. Integrate exact evidence and honest implementation status into OpenWarrant;
   regenerate projections, run record checks, machine-scope checks and full gate.
   Preserve failures and mark missing observations visibly.

Ownership: this Warrant owns OpenWarrant evidence publication; standard cookbook
owns provider code/tests. One shared adapter contract links both. No provider code
is vendored into OpenWarrant. Authorizations and legacy deliverable pins stay frozen.

Prompt permits unverified implementation; no paid calls, signing, self-verification
or publication. Local test success alone does not establish provider hosted CI or
common assurance. Roll back unaccepted code through Git; retain observation history.

# Assurance

### OBL-001 — provider retains owned dataset bytes
- **scope:** standard cookbook materialize_dataset_path and declared source identities.
- **evidence:** regression fails before fix; retained bytes survive source deletion;
  invalid input preserves previous output; symlink destination cannot redirect writes;
  provider checks pass at exact repair revision before integration.

### OBL-002 — original graph executes and invalid ports refuse
- **scope:** original OW47 three-record corpus and two-stage PlanSpec, one real local run.
- **evidence:** done status, both artifact receipts, equal expected bytes and external
  lineage reference; mapped port passes and incompatible kind refuses naming the port.

### OBL-003 — integration preserves provenance and history
- **scope:** new OW47 implementation records and this unsigned integration Warrant.
- **evidence:** original failures retained, signed sources unchanged, no lineage graph
  copied, projections/checks/full gate and exact machine-scope evidence pass. Unavailable
  provider checks remain visible and prevent integration completion claims.
